What is your opinion about patents?

Patenting an implementation : good idea.
Patenting a concept : bad idea.

We once lived in a world without patents and do you know what people would do? They would just keep everything secret to maintain control. No one, except a few select people, would get to know anything. Knowledge was not shared. That slowed down the progress of engineering and technology. Patents were invented as a means to make people share their secrets. The idea is you get a 20 year monopoly but have to reveal the inner workings of your idea(s).

So I see nothing wrong with the idea of a patent system. Out of all forms of intellectual property patents have the shortest life. It's 20 years which isn't actually that long at all, especially when you compare it to copyright, which is the life of the author plus 50 to 70 years. However, there are two problems with the patent system.

a) When people take a legitimately innovative idea, and slightly change it to circumvent patent protection.

b) People patent overly simplistic, and common ideas that should not have any protection. One example that comes to mind is the patent on mini games that you can play when a video game is loading. That was bullshit. First, the company granted that patent did not come up with the idea first, and two, the idea that you can own a patent on something that exhibits no form of genuine innovation is ridiculous.

I agree with you in the main, but patenting e.g.plants is, I think, morally wrong...some information should be freely available to all, But in the main, yes the patent system has improved development of technology while at the same time protecting the rights of the developer

Design patents and other newer, non-mechanical patents are so abused as to be counterproductive. People have patented everything from how to touch a cell phone screen to do a trivial and obvious task to patenting a series of yoga exercises.
I think patents are immoral under many reasonable moralities. I love earning them though.
